ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, where $\angle A=100^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in a circle, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle A + \angle C = 180^\circ$, \\
Since $\angle A = 100^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle C = 180^\circ - \angle A = 180^\circ - 100^\circ = \boxed{80^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, points A, B, C, D are all on the circumference, and are connected by line segments to form the inscribed quadrilateral ABCD. A is located at the lower left, B is located at the lower right, C is located on the right side, D is located at the upper left; therefore ∠A and ∠C are a pair of opposite angles of this cyclic quadrilateral. Reasoning: It is known that ∠A = 100°. The opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so ∠A + ∠C = 180°. Therefore ∠C = 180° - 100° = 80°.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the figure shows A, B, C, D lying on a common circle, with angle A formed by chords AD and AB, and angle C formed by chords CD and CB. From the text, angle A is 100°. Treat angle A as an inscribed angle intercepting the arc from D to B that does not contain A, which in the figure is the arc passing through C; that intercepted arc has measure 2 × 100° = 200°. The full circle is 360°, so the other arc from D to B, the one passing through A and B and not containing C, measures 360° - 200° = 160°. Angle C is an inscribed angle intercepting this remaining arc DB not containing C, so angle C = 160° / 2 = 80°.
method.CoT_raw:
